title: Work-energy lab
target: Compare measured work with kinetic-energy change.
criteria: Calculate kinetic energy from measured mass and speed.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: An example force-displacement graph is a rectangle at +6 N from x = 0 to 2.5 m. What work does its area represent?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An example force rises linearly from 0 to 12 N over 3 m. What is work under that force-displacement line?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A supplied trial uses mass 0.80 kg and speed 5.0 m/s. What kinetic energy follows?
cpa.guide: K = ½ × 0.80 × 25 = 10 J. These are supplied data, not a claim of student measurement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A supplied 1.5 kg cart slows from 4 to 2 m/s. What is its kinetic-energy change?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Measured net work and kinetic-energy change disagree beyond estimated uncertainty. Which next step is appropriate?
options: Check force sign, sensor calibration, all forces, and matching start/end intervals.
Replace measured values with model predictions.
Conclude energy was created without checking.
cpa.guide: A valid comparison requires consistent system, intervals, and measurements.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A force sensor records work from x = 0 to 2 m, but velocities are measured at x = 1 and 3 m. What is wrong with the comparison?
options: Work and ΔK refer to different motion intervals.
Work-energy requires a different mass at every point.
No correction is needed in any setup.
The speed readings must be identical.
cpa.guide: The theorem compares net work and kinetic-energy change over the same start and end states.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
